slot.subtopic: Basicity of amines in aqueous vs gas phase
slot.brief: Rank a set including aniline, ethylamine, guanidine-type and an amide-related nitrogen by basicity in water; must combine inductive, resonance and solvation effects.

stem: For guanidine, ethylamine, trimethylamine, aniline and acetamide, which pair gives the basicity order (strongest to weakest) in the gas phase and in water, respectively?
options: Gas: guanidine > trimethylamine > ethylamine > aniline > acetamide; water: guanidine > ethylamine > trimethylamine > aniline > acetamide
Gas: guanidine > ethylamine > trimethylamine > aniline > acetamide; water: guanidine > ethylamine > trimethylamine > aniline > acetamide
Gas: guanidine > trimethylamine > ethylamine > aniline > acetamide; water: guanidine > trimethylamine > ethylamine > aniline > acetamide
Gas: guanidine > trimethylamine > ethylamine > acetamide > aniline; water: guanidine > ethylamine > trimethylamine > acetamide > aniline

verdicts.working: Gas-phase proton affinity favors trimethylamine over ethylamine; in water, stronger solvation makes ethylamine more basic. Guanidine is strongest, while aniline is more basic than acetamide in both phases. This matches (A).

working:
In the gas phase, alkyl substitution raises proton affinity, so trimethylamine > ethylamine. In water, better solvation of ethylammonium reverses this pair. Guanidinium is resonance-stabilized; lone-pair delocalization weakens aniline and acetamide.

Independent check: Gas-phase proton affinity favors trimethylamine over ethylamine; in water, stronger solvation makes ethylamine more basic. Guanidine is strongest, while aniline is more basic than acetamide in both phases. This matches (A).
solution:
Guanidine is strongest due to resonance stabilization of guanidinium; resonance delocalization makes aniline and especially acetamide weaker bases.
In the gas phase, alkyl substitution increases proton affinity: $\text{trimethylamine}>\text{ethylamine}$.
In water, better solvation of ethylammonium reverses this order: $\text{ethylamine}>\text{trimethylamine}$.
Thus the respective orders are $\text{guanidine}>\text{trimethylamine}>\text{ethylamine}>\text{aniline}>\text{acetamide}$ and $\text{guanidine}>\text{ethylamine}>\text{trimethylamine}>\text{aniline}>\text{acetamide}$.
